text:
sophie: seeing recurring p95 east-west latency spikes between GPU nodes in us-west-2 during our midday batching window (11:30-12:15). started ~11:37. gnode pool-3, racks r3+r4. p95 normally ~12ms but spiking to 350-800ms intermittently. no big error rate increase, but tails are trash. did a quick ibv_devinfo and rdma counters look noisy. anyone seen this pattern?
raj-oncall: ack, i'm on it. are the affected pods colocated with other noisy CPU workloads? grabbing perf and tcpdump now.
sophie: not on noisy CPU hosts that I can tell; these are dedicated inference nodes. quick outputs i grabbed:
```
# ethtool -S eth0 | egrep "rx_errors|tx_errors|rx_nohandler"
rx_nohandler: 0
rx_errors: 4
tx_errors: 0
# ibv_devinfo -v | grep -E "link_layer|rate"
	phys_port_cnt: 1
	link_layer: InfiniBand
	link_speed: 100Gb/sec
# rdma_retrans: 12
# sample perf top during spike: softirq/irq handling heavy
```
alicia-net: sounds like NIC interrupt/coalescing behavior + RDMA completion storms. firmware on those NICs is 26.2 — we saw a coalescing regression in that build. can you paste `ethtool -c eth0`? also are we using sriov vf for the RDMA path or vfio?
sophie: ethtool coalesce shows rx-usecs 0 rx-frames 64 tx-usecs 500
ben-runtime: two quick possibilities: 1) kernel workqueue starvation causing recv path delay when batching bursts hit CPU; 2) GRO/GSO interacting poorly with small-packet RDMA fallbacks. can you check /proc/softirqs and dmesg for NAPI warnings?
maya-eval: we saw earlier that high batch concurrency + KV cache warmup leads to lots of small tail requests which increases packet rate and moves kernel out of optimal batching. disabling GRO on a host once reduced p95 in a past incident.
raj-oncall: i'm running a focused test:
- increase NIC coalescing rx-usecs to 200 on two nodes
- disable GRO on one of them (`ethtool -K eth0 gro off`)
- move 3 pods to r2 (different rack) to check rack-boundary effect
collecting p95 for next 15m.
infra-bot: automatic: deploy 3412345600 -> gnode-pool-3 paused due to latency anomaly (see signal eastwest.lat.p95 > 200ms).
alicia-net: also check MSI-X vector allocation; if vectors are shared between VF and PF we can get cross-traffic stalls. `lspci -vvv` will show if MSI-X is enabled per function. and verify irqbalance pinning or XPS is set correctly for the RDMA TX queues.
ben-runtime: on the runtime side i pushed a canary env to two hosts: `REDWOOD_BATCH_MAX=64` (was 256) and `BATCH_CONCURRENCY_TARGET=2`. aim is to smooth burstiness. if that lowers p95 we can consider a broader rollout or smarter adaptive batching.
sophie: ok thanks. i'll attach the pcap and perf flame after collection. early results: node A (gro off + coalescing 200) p95 dropped from 420ms -> 48ms within 5 minutes. node B (gro on, default coalesce) still spiking.
maya-eval: nice signal. worth trying bumping kernel wq max_active to 128 on one canary host too (`/proc/sys/net/core/wq_max_active`), we saw latency wins with more active wq threads under heavy softirq load.
raj-oncall: noted. i'm also toggling irq affinity to put RDMA/NIC interrupts on a dedicated CPU to avoid interfering with kworker. will report back after the 30m window.
sophie: plan ack: 1) keep coalesce=200 + gro=off on two canaries 2) move 6 pods off r3->r2 to test rack effect 3) collect 30m p95 and rdma counters 4) if stable -> escalate firmware rollback/firmware vendor ticket.
alicia-net: if firmware rollback isn't feasible, temporary mitigation: pin XPS, enforce SR-IOV VF isolation for RDMA VFs, and tune coalescing globally for pool-3. also open to trying newer driver with patched coalescing heuristics.
ben-runtime: thumbs up. if we do canary rollout, add telemetry for packet sizes distribution (histogram) so we can correlate small-packet bursts to p95.
raj-oncall: 20m into tests: node A steady p95 ~45ms, node B still has spikes up to 500ms at ~11:58. moving more traffic showed clear rack boundary effect — cross-rack flows worse. suspect NIC coalescing + IRQ steering + potential SR-IOV affinity mismatch.
sophie: thanks team. i'll log these results and attach traces to the incident ticket. will coordinate firmware rollback schedule if we confirm regression. :thumbsup:
